name: Tennr
description: Tennr is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Tennr is a privately held healthcare software company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $101 million Series C round announced on June 18, 2025, valued the company at $605 million.

Founded in 2021 and based in New York, Tennr develops AI software that reads incoming patient referrals and supporting records, many of them sent by fax, so that medical practices can schedule the patients they describe. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round.
round_notes: IVP led the Series C. In June 2025, Tennr said its revenue had more than tripled since its Series B the previous October; that figure is the company's own.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: IVP led the Series C, with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed Venture Partners, GV, ICONIQ, Foundation Capital and Frank Slootman, the former chief executive of Snowflake. Lightspeed led the Series B and Andreessen Horowitz the Series A. Other investors include The New Normal Fund and Y Combinator.
spv_sentence: No special purpose vehicles naming Tennr appear in SEC Form D filings.
sources: Sources: reports by Fortune (June 2025), SiliconANGLE (October 2024) and HIT Consultant (March 2024); and SEC Form D filings.
